property_summary: If the call to the external target fails, the contract C must not transfer out the received ETH (i.e., address(c).balance == 0 after go only when the external call succeeded).

After calling go with a positive value that the test contract can send, the call succeeds (does not revert) and C ends up with zero balance transferred out (i.e., address(c).balance == 0) — but the mutant that requires the external call to fail will revert the go call instead.

For any ether value sent to go, the call reverts whenever the external call to target would succeed (i.e., original requires external call success so go only proceeds when external call succeeds, but mutant reverts in that case).

For any amount sent to go, the call reverts exactly when the external call to target fails (i.e., reverted is true iff the external call failed), so the observed reverted flag equals the negation of whether the external call would succeed — original preserves this relation, the mutant inverts it.

For any caller and any payable amount, after go(...) completes the contract's owner address must have received any leftover balance (i.e., address(owner) balance increases by address(c).balance before the final transfer), but the mutant sends leftovers to msg.sender causing owner not to receive those funds for some inputs.

For every call to go(targeting a callee that accepts the forwarded msg.value and does not re-enter), the reference contract always sends any remaining contract balance to its owner (owner's balance increases by that remaining amount), whereas the mutant instead sends the remaining balance to msg.sender, breaking this invariant for some caller/address/amount combinations.

For any caller and any sent value, if the external callee reverts the forwarded call, the reference contract forwards the remaining contract balance to its owner (so owner balance increases), whereas the mutant sends that remaining balance to msg.sender, breaking this property for some caller inputs.

For any caller and any nonzero ETH amount sent to go when the callee accepts the forwarded call but then leaves a nonzero residual balance in C (e.g. callee forwards the funds elsewhere), C always transfers its remaining balance to its stored owner, whereas the mutant transfers that remaining balance to msg.sender — so the owner balance increases after go() in the reference but may not in the mutant.

For every admissible call where the callee accepts plain Ether (does not revert) and C holds any leftover balance after forwarding msg.value, the reference always transfers that leftover to the stored owner address; the mutant instead transfers leftover to msg.sender, so there exists a caller and amount for which the owner's balance does not increase (violating the rule).

For every call to go() with any nonnegative msg.value, contract C forwards the full msg.value onwards so that after go() completes the contract balance is zero (owner receives all forwarded remaining balance); the mutant that only forwards half leaves a nonzero contract balance for some inputs, violating this property.

For every nonzero ether payment to go(), contract C forwards the full msg.value to the external target and ends with zero balance (owner receives remaining balance); the mutant that only forwards half can leave a nonzero contract balance after go() for some payment amounts.

For any caller and any amount >=1 wei sent to go, the reference C always ends with address(c).balance == 0 after go() completes (it forwards all msg.value to target then transfers remaining balance to owner); the mutant that only forwards half can leave address(c).balance > 0 for some msg.value and thus violates this rule.

For every caller and every msg.value, calling go() on the reference forwards msg.value to the external target (so the target receives exactly msg.value) and then owner receives any leftover, whereas the mutant that forwards only half can cause the target to receive strictly less than msg.value for some fuzzed msg.value and thus violates the equality of the target-received amount to msg.value.

For every nonzero msg.value and for any callee that accepts Ether (does not revert), the reference C ends with address(c).balance == 0 after go() completes (it forwards all msg.value to the target and transfers any remaining balance to owner); the mutant that only forwards half can leave address(c).balance > 0 for some msg.value, so the property will fail for that mutant.
